questions.question: A reply takes 3.2s to generate, and streaming shows the first token at 0.5s. What did streaming improve?
options: Time to first token, i.e. how soon the user sees something
questions.explanation: The model is no faster overall. Streaming delivers output as it's produced, so perceived latency drops.

questions.question: What marks the end of one SSE event?
questions.explanation: Events end at an empty line. One event can contain several data: lines, joined with \n.

questions.question: Why does chunk.decode("utf-8") on each network chunk sometimes crash?
options: A multi-byte character like ✅ can be split across two chunks; use an incremental decoder
questions.explanation: Chunks are arbitrary byte ranges. An incremental decoder holds incomplete bytes until the rest arrive.

questions.question: How are streamed tool-call fragments put back together?
options: Each fragment is a complete JSON object
By index: the first fragment has the id and name, later ones append argument text, parsed as JSON only at the end
questions.explanation: Fragments for parallel calls interleave, so group them by index and parse arguments after the stream finishes.

questions.question: In 1 of 4 live runs, llama3.2 streamed its tool call as plain text with broken JSON. What's the right response?
options: Detect tool-shaped text, validate it against the schema, and either convert it or return an error observation, because small models fail intermittently
questions.explanation: Intermittent failures need handling in the loop, not hope. Validation decides whether the text is safe to treat as a call.

questions.question: Your streamed responses never include token usage. Most likely fix?
questions.explanation: OpenAI-style streams only send a final usage chunk when asked via include_usage.
